scenario.name: CISA AA25-071A & Palo Alto Unit 42 — Medusa Ransomware: ScreenConnect RMM, gaze.exe (ThrottleStop.sys) Kernel Callback Killer & PDQ Deploy Encryption
scenario.overview: Picture a busy downtown bank branch with marble teller windows, brass counter bars, and a heavy circular steel vault at the rear. At the front marble counter, a visitor wearing a borrowed courier coat hands the bank teller an official-looking transfer slip to slip past the velvet queue. In this real-world scenario, the intruder moves quietly past the brass teller window into neighboring restricted rooms, then smuggles copied records out past the brass teller window in tiny disguised batches. Only when the branch manager reviews the vault camera footage alongside the teller receipt book does the unauthorized vault visit stand out immediately. In this scenario (T1190, CISA AA25-071A & Palo Alto Unit 42, Medusa Ransomware: ScreenConnect RMM, gaze.exe , ThrottleStop.sys Kernel Callback Killer & PDQ Deploy Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: screenConnect RMM Foothold, Advanced IP, then gaze.exe Loading Signed ThrottleStop.sys, then pDQ Deploy Mass Distribution, VSS Deletion. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ScreenConnect RMM Foothold, Advanced IP, then gaze.exe Loading Signed ThrottleStop.sys, then PDQ Deploy Mass Distribution, VSS Deletion. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: PDQ Deploy Mass Distribution, VSS Deletion & `.medusa` AES-256-CBC Encryption
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement & Impact (T1072 - Software Deployment Tools / T1486)
stages.description: With the heavy steel vault door swung wide open, the intruder packs high-value ledger folders into a satchel while the front lobby appears completely calm. In this final step inside the bank branch, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the brass teller window in tiny disguised batches until the branch vault camera & ledger catches the mismatch. Using PDQ Deploy (PDQDeployConsole.exe) or psexec.exe -s, the operator pushes the Medusa encryptor (gaze.exe / medusa.exe) across all domain hosts. Medusa terminates over 280 backup, database, and mail services (vss, sql, veeam, sophos), runs vssadmin Delete Shadows /all /quiet, deletes C:\*.vhd, and encrypts files with AES-256-CBC + RSA-2048 (.medusa and !!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt) (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with DistributionMechanism=PDQ Deploy / PsExec Domain Push, RansomNote=!!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt, EncryptedExtension=.medusa so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes vssadmin.exe Delete Shadows /all /quiet && wbadmin.exe delete catalog -quiet (which executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet , or WMI Win32_ShadowCopy.Delete to invoke IVssBackupComponents::DeleteSnapshots and purge all exi so that inhibits system recovery , T1072 during "PDQ Deploy Mass Distribution, VSS Deletion & .medusa AES-256-CBC Encryption" by destroying local disk shadow copies before or after payload execution so defenders cannot roll back encrypted files or inspect historical volume state). Next, the follow-up artifact wmic.exe process where name="sqlservr.exe" call terminate && del /s /f /q C:\*.vhd E:\*.bac runs (which invokes the Windows Management Instrumentation command-line interface , wmic.exe or DCOM/WinRM provider host , wmiprvse.exe to execute Win32_Proces so that executes lateral movement or local process creation , T1072 via the trusted WMI provider daemon , wmiprvse.exe during "PDQ Deploy Mass Distribution, VSS Deletion & .medusa AES-256-CBC Encryption" to decouple the child process parent PID from the attacker's session). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ gaze.exe / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 gaze.exe Kernel Killer (ThrottleStop.sys)) to Node ④ (#4 PDQ Deploy / PsExec Distribution Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise Fleet (.medusa AES-256-CBC)).

wmic.exe process where name="sqlservr.exe" call terminate && del /s /f /q C:\*.vhd E:\*.bac
Require tiered administrative accounts for software deployment consoles (PDQ Deploy, SCCM) and block `del /s /f /q *.vhd` and `wbadmin delete catalog` via EDR.
Lateral Movement & Impact (T1072 - Software Deployment Tools / T1486)
